newsitem.title: UK: Liberty says provisions taken adequate.
newsitem.headline: Liberty says provisions taken adequate.

text.p: Liberty Plc, the British retailer known for its fine fabrics, on Friday said it believes the provisions it took last year for its restructuring programme remain adequate.

Liberty reported pretax profit for the first half ended July 27 of 1.1 million stg, compared to year-ago profit of 275,000 stg. No interim dividend was declared. Turnover edged down to 39.0 million from 39.3 million a year-ago.

"We remain confident that the provisions made last year will prove adequate for the restructuring programme and that the more focused management structure will produce increasing benefits from our profitable ongoing operations," chairman Denis Cassidy said in a statement.
"The board is also confident that it will accelerate this progress in the second half and will have a more appropriate base on which to determine dividend policy by the year end," he said.
Liberty said that under its restructuring programme all its UK provincial branches, the Oxford Collection and the Muji store in Glasgow have been closed.
